copy.summary: Plays a tone at the pitch you set
copy.wiringNote: Wire S to the GPIO and - to ground; leave the middle pin unconnected (Joy-IT labels it +V, but the buzzer sounds without it). The controller plays a square wave at Pitch while Sound is true, and the pin rests low otherwise. It is loudest near 2 kHz. It draws 25 mA or less straight from the pin; if your buzzer reads a few tens of ohms on a meter rather than open, it is a coil type and needs a transistor. One passive buzzer per board: the tone generator drives one pin at a time.
